stemMd:
A researcher studying an old irrigation network finds that its channels were repeatedly rerouted. Earlier descriptions had treated the network as a single ingenious design. The new evidence instead suggests a sequence of local adjustments made as fields, labor, and water availability changed.

Which choice best states the main idea?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Every rerouting made the network less effective.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The channels were never used to carry water.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The network may be better understood as an evolving response to changing conditions than as one fixed plan.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The earlier descriptions accurately captured all stages.

explanationMd: Repeated rerouting supports a developmental account. The contrast is between a unified original plan and cumulative adaptation, not between useful and useless irrigation.

distractorRationale.a: The text does not rank the adjustments' effectiveness.
distractorRationale.d: The new evidence revises the single-design account.
